constraints.text: found near the American River ... James Marshall ... scooped yellow stones from the riverbed
constraints.reading: The featured item and the chapter's central imagery are tied to a RIVER and a RIVERBED. Charitably, the hiding spot may sit near flowing water / a watercourse, at or beside a riverbank where one would scoop or reach low.

constraints.text: the most significant memorial is the James Marshall Monument ... a hilltop tomb topped by a bronze statue of Marshall holding a nugget and pointing toward the discovery spot
constraints.reading: Strong spatial image of a HILLTOP feature with a long downward view, and a statue that POINTS toward a specific lower spot. Generically: a high point overlooking a lower target, with a directional 'pointer' landmark aiming at the actual location.

constraints.text: a bronze statue of Marshall ... pointing toward the discovery spot
constraints.reading: A literal directional cue: an object/landmark that points the way. The hiding spot may lie in the direction a marker, statue, or natural feature 'points' rather than at the marker itself.

constraints.text: the tailrace of Sutter's Mill ... gold flakes in the tailrace
constraints.reading: A tailrace is a narrow water channel/sluice exiting a mill. Generically suggests a constricted flowing-water channel or man-made-looking water passage as a possible nearby feature.

constraints.text: river dams to expose the sandy bed ... gold pans ... gravel
constraints.reading: Placer-gold imagery (sandy/gravel bed, where heavy material settles). Charitably: look low in a gravel/sand pocket, a streambed depression, where small heavy things collect, rather than high on a slope.

constraints.text: discovered during a leisurely afternoon outing in which you enjoy a picnic with a loved one
constraints.reading: Implies the spot is in a pleasant, calm, accessible setting suitable for a picnic — likely an open, gentle, view-friendly public area near a road, not a rugged or hidden crevice.

constraints.text: no need to ... sleep on dusty ground ... no rations or survival kits ... no water crossings, no danger
constraints.reading: Reinforces a benign, easy-to-reach surface location: no water crossing required to reach it, no scrambling — a spot you can simply walk up to and stand at.

constraints.text: a very large California Gold Rush gold nugget weighing over twenty-one ounces ... a Californian nugget this size is very rare
constraints.reading: The object is a NUGGET — a rounded, irregular, lumpy gold-colored stone. Charitably, the hiding place may itself resemble or sit beside a pale/golden rounded boulder or knob (a nugget-shaped landform echo).

constraints.text: roughly forty miles east ... ninety miles west ... 40 miles east of Sacramento
constraints.reading: Chapter repeatedly uses fixed cardinal-direction distances (east/west) measured from a known anchor point. Generically supports the idea of measuring a distance and direction from a recognizable reference landmark to reach the target.

constraints.text: Sutter Buttes ... a striking small mountain range
constraints.reading: Mention of a small isolated mountain/buttes rising from flatter land — a possible echo of a distinctive standalone high feature, though the page flags it as private and deprioritized.

constraints.text: Calistoga ... ringed by accessible public land (Mount Saint Helena ... Oat Hill Mine Trail)
constraints.reading: References to a town encircled by mountains/trails — a high overlook (Mount Saint Helena) above a valley. Generically: a high vantage over a basin as a candidate spatial setting.

constraints.text: placer gold collects ... below riffles and bends; the heavy things settle where moving water slows — the inside of a bend
constraints.reading: (Thematic/imagery only — not stated as a poem.) Where water bends and slows, heavy things settle low. Charitably suggests checking the inside of a bend / a slack low pocket beside flowing water for the resting place.
